t: #2587 — Rearrange Array to Maximize Prefix Score
o: Rearrange nums so that as many prefix sums as possible are strictly positive. For [2,-1,0,1,-3,3,-3] the order [2,3,1,0,-1,-3,-3] keeps six prefixes positive. For [-2,-3,0] no prefix can ever be positive, so the score is 0. Greedy ordering by value is clearly best: big positives first, then smaller ones, then negatives from least negative to most negative.
k: Placing larger elements earlier maximizes every prefix sum simultaneously (an exchange argument shows sorting descending is optimal).
Once the running sum plus the next (largest remaining) element is ≤ 0, no later element can help, so we can stop.
Zeros count toward the score whenever the running sum is already positive.

a.n: Approach 1: Sort descending and take greedily
a.i: Sort nums in descending order and accumulate a running sum, counting each element that keeps the sum strictly positive. Stop at the first element that would make the sum non-positive — because the array is sorted, every subsequent element is ≤ the current one and would also fail.
s: Iterate keeping a running sum; increment the count when sum + x > 0, updating the sum.
Break at the first failure and return the count.
a.t: O(n log n) — sorting dominates; the scan is linear.
a.sp: O(1) extra (in-place sort), or O(n) depending on the sort.

w: Why descending is optimal: swapping any two adjacent elements so the larger comes first never decreases any prefix sum, so the sorted order maximizes the count of positive prefixes for every prefix length simultaneously. Pitfall: using sum + x >= 0 instead of > 0 (prefixes must be strictly positive), and forgetting that zeros are beneficial once the sum is positive. Follow-up: maximize the number of positive prefixes subject to a fixed first element.
